title: mini-orchestrator-playbook: per-request model chooser (scratchpad)
body:
Goal / thesis:

Sketching a small "mini-orchestrator" service that lives near the API edge and cheaply picks the best-serving model variant for each inference request based on signals (prompt fingerprint, user QoS tier, per-request budget, recent evals). Objective is to reduce unit cost and tail latency regressions while preserving quality for hard prompts. This is a personal scratchpad — lots of open questions.

Why now:
- We have multiple compatible model variants (full-precision, quantized, distilled, short-context) in the catalog.
- Customers want cost predictability and better out-of-the-box SLOs.
- Many failures/quality drops are avoidable if we route a small fraction of requests to more expensive variants.

High-level concept:
- A lightweight sidecar/proxy (mini-orch) intercepts requests (hosted and Dedicated edge) and computes a routing decision in <1ms median.
- Decision inputs: prompt fingerprint (hash + features), recent micro-evals for similar prompts, user/tenant QoS tier, explicit per-request budget tag, current capacity signals (fallback if hot), and model performance profiles (latency/cost/accuracy buckets).
- Output: select model variant id + explainability tag (why routed), and optionally attach a micro-eval hook for probabilistic sampling to update offline eval sets.

Core capabilities (MVP):
1) Feature extractor: cheap fingerprint (n-gram sketch, token-length, special token markers).
2) Policy store: per-tenant routing policies (default, conservative, frugal).
3) Decision function: rules + lightweight scoring model (logistic reg over features) that returns {variant, reason, sample_for_eval?}.
4) Telemetry: per-decision stats (chosen variant, latency, token usage, note if fallback triggered).
5) Feedback loop: sampled responses go into a micro-eval pipeline to update the policy model weekly.

User stories (rough):
- As a small SaaS app, I want default frugal routing so 90% of requests use cheaper variants and 10% use full models for edge quality, so my monthly bill is stable.
- As a platform engineer, I want per-tenant override so enterprise customers can pin all traffic to a specific variant.
- As an SRE, I want a fallback path that automatically selects lower-latency variants when a region experiences capacity pressure.
- As an ML researcher, I want sampled micro-evals to collect hard examples so we can improve the scoring model.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Routing decision latency <= 2 ms p50, <= 10 ms p99.
- End-to-end token cost reduced by >= 12% for frugal default tenants without measurable decrease in a selected quality metric on held-out prompts.
- Telemetry pipeline ingests routing labels and correlates with per-request final quality (where available).
- Feature flags to turn off sampling and to force default variant.

Proposed experiments (first 6 weeks):
- A/B: baseline (no-orch) vs mini-orch frugal policy on a set of non-critical tenants to measure cost delta and user-visible regressions.
- Micro-eval cadence test: daily vs weekly sampling — measure signal-to-noise and whether weekly is sufficient for policy retraining.
- Conservative policy band: increase sampling probability for requests flagged as 'complex' (longer token-length, many instructions) and see effect on quality/cost.

Metrics to track:
- Cost per 1k requests (pre/post) per tenant segment.
- Quality delta on micro-eval set (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-eval metric chosen) and fraction of user complaints / support tickets.
- Decision latency distribution.
- Fraction sampled for micro-eval and efficacy of sampling (fraction of sampled requests that produce a model-choice change on retraining).

Implementation notes / stack:
- Lightweight Go sidecar for latency; exposes a local RPC (gRPC) used by the API gateway.
- Policy store in an existing config service (feature flag + per-tenant JSON).
- Scoring model: start with a small sklearn-ish logistic/regression (serialized) served in-process; later consider tiny neural net with ONNX runtime if needed.
- Micro-eval writes to the existing eval bucket with a sample tag.

Risks and unknowns:
- Policy oscillation: frequent retraining or environment changes could flip a tenant's routing back-and-forth causing instability. Need smoothing and versioned policies.
- Cold prompts: fingerprinting might misclassify novel queries; robust fallback and conservative sampling required.
- Privacy: fingerprinting must avoid storing PII; use hashed/sketch features and TTL'd ephemeral keys.
- Observability: need to attribute cost savings to the correct routing decisions — careful instrumentation required.

Open questions / things to decide:
- Should an opt-in tenant get a rollout-only sampling mode (i.e., all traffic continues to chosen variant but copy decisions to mini-orch)? Pros/cons.
- What exact feature set for fingerprinting provides best signal vs cost? (token-length, instruction count, presence of code blocks, numeric entities?).
- How aggressive should the default frugal policy be? 70/30 vs 90/10? Let experiments decide, but choose safe default (80/20).
- Retraining cadence: weekly looks reasonable but depends on sampling volume.

Immediate TODOs (notes to self):
- Prototype extractor in Python to see initial separability on historical logs (target: within 2 days).
- Add a simple routing tag in hosted-api proxy to mark decisions (instrumentation ticket).
- Mock small policy store and run 1k synthetic requests through the prototype to measure latency.
- Sync with Mika for micro-eval ingestion format and Samir for privacy constraints.

Notes / stray thoughts (informal):
- Could reuse existing model profiles from Console (latency/cost buckets) rather than duplicating.
- If sidecar proves too slow, consider moving to policy-as-config in gateway with precomputed hash tables for hot prompts.
- Nice-to-have: human-readable "reason" that shows in Console for a routing decision to help debug customer reports.

Backlinks / references I should read again:
- ticket: MOD-197 (model profiles and cost buckets)
- confluence: "Sampling-for-micro-evals" (design doc by ML-ops)
- internal slack thread: #model-routing-discussion (Dec 2024)

Last quick sketch of API contract (local RPC):
Request: { prompt_sketch, tenant_id, qos_tag, explicit_budget_tag? }
Response: { variant_id, reason_code, sample_for_eval: bool, policy_version }

End of scratchpad — keep this intentionally rough. Will tidy after first prototype results.

-- Irene
(quick note: if rewriting as a PRD, move acceptance criteria to measurable KPIs section and add rollout plan with safety gates)
